text:
Maria: heads-up — NF4/FP4 canary (v3.2.1) at 10% shows a consistent throughput drop and memory surge on canary-A nodes. I'm dumping notes and a short log excerpt below.

Maria: log tail from worker-12: 
```
[2026-03-17T22:14:02Z] WARNING kernel_selector: chosen kernel=generic_int4 (fallback) for model=gptx-13b seq=1024 batch=4
[2026-03-17T22:14:03Z] ERROR allocator: cudaMalloc failed size=2147483648 (2GB)
[2026-03-17T22:14:03Z] INFO kv_cache: entries=1.3M shards=8 slab_bytes=14.2G
```

Ajay: saw this on canary-B as well. latency p50 -> p95 widened and throughput dropped ~30% for long-seq traffic. nvprof shows a lot of small `cudaMalloc`/`cudaFree` churn when the generic kernel path is used.

Lia: adding what I saw from calibration: our nf4 calibrator for this model produced a few outlier scales on mid layers. example: `layer27_calib: mean_scale=0.34, 99p_scale=1.72` — that inflates activations after quant-dequant round trips. probably explains the bigger slabs.

Tom: are we certain this is kernel-selection-related and not a packing/packing change in the runtime? we switched batcher heuristics last week.

Maria: mix of both imo. kernel selector pulled a kernel optimized for smaller seqs because the batcher histogram we feed it collapsed different seq-length buckets. when that kernel hit long seq requests it did a lot more temporary buffer allocation (KV materialization) -> cache fragmentation.

Sam: reproducer on staging: run this workload (long prefix + streaming) against canary kernel vs stable kernel. command: `rd-infer profile --target canary-A --trace-kernel-selection --workload long-seq-stream`

Sam: profile snippet (staging): 
```
profile: tokens 50-5000
chosen kernel: generic_int4 when batcher_hist(seq>512) weighted avg < 0.4
nvprof: cudaMalloc count=3128 vs 42 on stable path
kv stats: live_entries=1.1M -> slab fragmentation up 48%
```

Ajay: that `batcher_hist` collapse is the key. we aggregate by time-window not seq-bucket, so bursts of short sessions pollute the histogram. kernel selector thought short-opt kernel is best.

Lia: calibration + selector combo is the dangerous intersection. NF4/FP4 kernels are more sensitive to per-layer scale shifts; fallback generic kernels allocate extra temporary tensors rather than streaming into preallocated buffers.

Tom: immediate actions:
- rollback canary percentage to 1% (DevOpsBot?)
- add seq-length bucketing to the kernel selector input (Ajay/Lia)
- add a clamp on per-layer calib scale diffs to avoid extreme calibration jumps (Lia)
- add a metric for `cudaMalloc_count` and `kv_slab_fragmentation` to the canary dashboard (Sam)

DevOpsBot: rolling canary from 10% -> 1% now. will post when done. :white_check_mark:

RuntimeBot: canary rollback complete on canary-A/canary-B. traffic reduced to 1% at 2026-03-17T22:21:49Z.

Sam: I'll add the malloc_count alert and a short grafana panel for fragmentation. linking perf dashboard once done.

Ajay: I'll prototype seq-bucketed histograms today and wire into kernel-selector. high-level change: keep separate latency/throughput histograms per seq-range (0-64,65-256,257-1024,1025+). selector will prefer kernels with good metrics in the appropriate bucket.

Lia: I'll add a soft-clamp in calibration: if new scale > 3x old_scale then clamp to 1.5x and emit a calibration-anomaly event. this avoids huge activation blowups during noisy calibrations.

Maria: thanks all. postmortem checklist: repro steps (Sam), quick rollback doc (Tom), selector change PR (Ajay), calibrator patch (Lia). if anyone hits other canary nodes pls ping here. :pray:
